note: Controlled relation vocabulary. Every relation must name its type, its direction and the conditions that bound it. A relation whose types violate the signature is rejected (QC-03); a relation whose supporting quote is not verbatim in the cited paragraph is rejected outright.

relations.definition: The subject employs the object as an instrument, technique, material, or procedure.
relations.reject_when: the sentence only lists the term among others, or the object appears only in the introduction as background

relations.definition: The subject is explicitly set against the object on a stated basis.
relations.reject_when: two things merely co-occur in the text; no comparative wording and no shared basis

relations.definition: The subject is asserted to be better than the object, on a named metric or task.
relations.reject_when: the improvement is stated for a different metric, sample, or condition than the one being claimed; a bare adjective with the basis missing

relations.definition: The subject is offered as evidence for the object conclusion.
relations.reject_when: the paper reports the observation but draws no conclusion, or the support is only asserted in a review sentence

relations.definition: The subject is stated to conflict with the object.
relations.reject_when: 'however' introduces a new topic rather than a conflicting claim; both sides are not quoted

relations.definition: The subject produces a numeric or categorical value for the object metric.
relations.reject_when: no value or unit can be found in the quoted span, so the metric is only named, not measured

relations.definition: The subject is applied to the object material in order to reveal its properties.
relations.reject_when: the material is only the sample holder or the substrate of a different measurement

evidence_strength.definition: The quoted sentence states the relation in its own words; no inference needed.
The relation is carried by a caption, table cell, or figure label rather than running prose.
The relation needs one stated premise beyond the quote; the premise must be recorded in `basis`.
The relation is a model reading that the text does not state. Allowed only if flagged, and it downgrades the run to partial.
